title: Xiaomi Has a Luxury SUV for $31,000 That All Western Brands Should Fear
gist: Xiaomi Auto priced its SkyNomad extended-range SUVs at RMB 209,900 (about $31,000) for the five-seat N70 Pro and RMB 299,900 (about $44,700) for the seven-seat N90 Max Studio camper, packing lidar, Nvidia's Thor-U chip, a reconfigurable Kunlun flat-floor platform and a claimed 1,000-mile combined range into the price of a Hyundai Tucson. With Xiaomi entering Europe in 2027 and the Jaecoo 7 already a UK best-seller at £29,210, the piece argues Western premium SUV makers are underestimating a segment that is nearly half of global new car sales.

themes.theme: SUV segment is the whole battlefield

insights.claim: SUVs account for nearly half of all new car sales worldwide, making them by a wide margin the largest segment in the global auto industry and therefore the segment where share loss hurts incumbents most.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Any Chinese entrant that wins SUV share is attacking the profit pool that funds Western automakers' entire EV transition, not a niche.
insights.quote: Accounting for nearly half of all new sales worldwide, this is by some margin the largest segment in the global auto industry.
insights.locator: If there's one thing that can unite

insights.claim: Trucks and SUVs represent more than 80 percent of new vehicle sales in America, while Ford no longer sells a traditional sedan in the US at all and only about a third of Chinese autos are sedans.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: US demand is structurally concentrated in the heaviest, most power-hungry body styles, which sets the battery and range bar any importer must clear.
insights.quote: Trucks and SUVs represent more than 80 percent of new vehicle sales in America these days.

insights.claim: Schaeffler Group US CEO Marc McGrath says a main reason the supplier is developing its own solid-state batteries is to properly electrify the power-hungry trucks and SUVs American buyers prefer, with the failed F-150 Lightning ramp as the cautionary case.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Tier-one suppliers are betting solid-state is the unlock for US electrification economics; watch supplier battery programs as a leading indicator of OEM timelines.
insights.quote: No one wants another F-150 Lightning U-turn.
insights.locator: Marc McGrath, US CEO of the automotive manufacturer Schaeffler Group

insights.claim: The Chinese-made Jaecoo 7 went from unknown newcomer in 2025 to one of the UK's best-selling new cars, nicknamed the "Temu Range Rover" and priced at £29,210, roughly $39,000, in both gas and hybrid versions.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Proof that a sub-£30k Chinese SUV can take mass-market share in a Western market inside a single model year, compressing the timeline for incumbent share loss.
insights.quote: going from an unknown newcomer in 2025 to now being one of the country’s best-selling new cars
insights.locator: The shocking success of the Jaecoo 7

insights.claim: The author's local Nissan dealer dropped the Japanese brand outright and converted to an official Jaecoo dealership selling the 7, 5 and 8, showing the channel itself is defecting, not just consumers.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Dealer conversions are a hard-to-reverse structural loss; track franchise-network churn in the UK as an early warning for legacy brand volumes.
insights.quote: My local Nissan dealer has swiftly dumped the Japanese brand and is now an official Jaecoo dealer
insights.locator: These 7s are becoming ubiquitous on UK roads

insights.claim: Xiaomi Auto is set to launch in Europe in 2027 despite building its first EV only in 2024, and its SU7 Ultra claimed the title of world's fastest sedan in that same debut year.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: A three-year path from first vehicle to credible European premium entrant shows consumer-electronics development cadence now applies to cars.
insights.quote: the big one incoming is Xiaomi Auto, set to launch in Europe in 2027, despite only making its first EV in 2024
insights.locator: Other Chinese brands are playing the same tactic in Europe

insights.claim: XPeng and BYD are running the same European SUV-led entry tactic as Jaecoo, meaning incumbents face a coordinated multi-brand wave rather than a single challenger.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Defensive tariff or pricing responses aimed at one brand will not stem the flow; the exposure is sector-wide for European volume and premium makers.
insights.locator: Other Chinese brands are playing the same tactic in Europe

themes.theme: Product spec gap versus Western flagships

insights.claim: The Xiaomi SkyNomad N70 is a five-seat extended-range EV that the reviewer says has better technology than a Range Rover at half the price of a Range Rover Velar, and in Stealth Black Edition trim closely mimics Range Rover styling.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: If the tech-per-dollar claim holds in Europe, premium brand pricing power, not just volume share, is at risk.
insights.quote: has better technology than a Range Rover at half the price of a Velar

insights.claim: The SkyNomad's Kunlun platform delivers a flat floor with sliding rails from the front seats to the boot, front seats that spin a full 180 degrees, movable center console and rear legroom that maxes out at over five feet.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Interior reconfigurability is a packaging advantage that dedicated EV/EREV architectures enable and adapted legacy platforms cannot easily match.
insights.locator: The theme of reconfigurable interiors continues

insights.claim: By comparison, cutting-edge interior innovation on Western flagship models amounts to power doors, massage seats, scent sprays and a center console that moves maybe 10 cm, which the reviewer calls lazy.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: The competitive gap is in feature velocity, not just cost; Western premium R&D productivity is the variable to scrutinize.
insights.quote: The SkyNomad makes US and European efforts look, frankly, lazy
insights.locator: Just stop for a minute and compare

insights.claim: The SkyNomad ships lidar units, high-definition cameras and Nvidia's Thor-U chip for level 2-plus autonomous control, putting frontier autonomy silicon into a roughly $31,000 vehicle.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Lidar and high-end compute at entry-luxury prices compresses the bill-of-materials premium Western ADAS programs still charge for.

insights.claim: The SkyNomad's extended-range powertrain pairs a 1.5-liter turbocharged combustion generator that never drives the wheels with dual electric motors, charges 20 to 80 percent in as little as 18 minutes, and claims 300-plus miles electric-only and 1,000 miles combined on China's CLTC cycle, about 700 miles under stricter US EPA standards.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: EREV architecture sidesteps charging-infrastructure risk in export markets, which is why it is the likely wedge product for Western entry.
insights.quote: 1,000-mile combined range. Yes, these stats use China’s far more forgiving CLTC cycle, but this converts to about 700 miles using stricter US EPA standards.

insights.claim: A low-voltage power system holds SkyNomad sentry-mode drain to under 5 kilometers of range overnight while an onboard fridge drawing 0.72 kWh a day runs up to 24 hours continuously, an energy-efficiency detail Western EVs rarely quantify.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Parasitic-drain engineering is an under-covered differentiator that shapes real-world ownership cost and reviewer scores.
insights.locator: A low-voltage power system apparently keeps “sentry mode” drain

insights.claim: Xiaomi offers in-brand car-to-car communication on the SkyNomad that runs over cellular coverage rather than short-range radio and is marketed as having unlimited range, reusing technology Xiaomi already ships in its phones.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Phone-to-car feature transfer is a concrete example of consumer-electronics ecosystem leverage that pure-play automakers cannot replicate cheaply.
insights.locator: An amazing optional extra for the SkyNomad

insights.claim: The entry-level SkyNomad N70 Pro, a rear-wheel-drive five-seater with lidar and a 14-speaker system, is priced at RMB 209,900 or just over $31,000, about the same as a 2026 Hyundai Tucson, while the maxed-out N90 Max Studio camper is RMB 299,900 or about $44,700.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: The price anchor sits at mainstream compact-SUV level, so the pricing threat is to volume brands as well as to premium marques.
insights.quote: The entry-level N70 Pro five-seat, rear-wheel-drive model with its movable “Italian sofa” seats, lidar, 14-speaker sound system including subwoofer and headrest speakers, and prodigious range is just RMB 209,900, or just over $31,000
insights.locator: Now to the clincher: the price

insights.claim: A Western luxury auto CEO asked about Xiaomi Auto laughed and scoffed that the company makes vacuums, a dismissal the author compares to Elon Musk laughing off BYD as a competitor in a 2011 Bloomberg interview.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Incumbent dismissal is itself the signal: the BYD analogy implies management teams are mispricing the entrant risk in guidance and capital allocation.
insights.quote: “They make vacuums, don't they?” he scoffed.
insights.locator: Earlier this month, I asked a Western luxury auto CEO

insights.claim: Bentley and Range Rover have both revealed flagship electric SUVs, but the author argues they should be worried about how many sales Xiaomi's SkyNomad line takes from them.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Flagship EV launches at the top of the market may land into direct price-undercutting from a Chinese entrant within two years.
insights.locator: Bentley and Range Rover may well have revealed
